requires: Context, permission, provider behavior, scope statement or introduction; its operative requirements are in the normative continuations. The same call (the same provider, operation and arguments) made again less than one second after a 429 for it was answered is answered 429 again.

requires: Handle the provider guarantee of no more than three consecutive 429s and its four-open-session exception; reconcile that guarantee with the preceding one-second cooldown rule.
observe: Inspect retry timestamps and outcomes under scripted 429s, including a fourth identical attempt before one second and session-cap refusals; use the foreman ruling for any disputed provider guarantee.
readings: The three-429 maximum overrides the cooldown rule on attempt four, so that attempt must be non-429 even if made too early.
The maximum applies to attempts that respect the cooldown; attempts less than one second after the previous 429 can still receive 429 and do not advance that guarantee.

requires: Exclude actual waits before retries after a 429 from the inherited 10-second fast-provider build bound.
observe: Script independent throttles on multiple calls, measure retry-wait time and total elapsed build time, then compare non-wait duration to ten seconds.

requires: Context, permission, provider behavior, scope statement or introduction; its operative requirements are in the normative continuations. ## The selection rule
observe: No independent service assertion; apply its normative continuations and use provider behaviors as test conditions.

requires: Context, permission, provider behavior, scope statement or introduction; its operative requirements are in the normative continuations. Rank a field's candidates, highest first, by:
observe: No independent service assertion; apply its normative continuations and use provider behaviors as test conditions.

requires: Context, permission, provider behavior, scope statement or introduction; its operative requirements are in the normative continuations. **Authority** of the page's kind:
observe: No independent service assertion; apply its normative continuations and use provider behaviors as test conditions.

requires: Rank own and filing equally highest, then news, then aggregator, with imported null kind equal to aggregator.
observe: Construct authority/recency conflicts and verify authority wins before any newer lower-authority candidate.

requires: Within equal authority, rank later publication instants higher; do not invent a restriction that valid future publication times are undated.
observe: Use older/newer/future dates and equivalent instants with different RFC3339 offsets; verify time ordering before URL/provider/value ties.

requires: Within equal authority, rank every valid dated candidate above undated candidates.
observe: Compare old valid dates, null dates and malformed-header dates.

requires: After authority and publication ties, sort URLs ascending by Unicode code point; for equal URLs sort provider nimble,tavily,kernel,browserbase.
observe: Construct URL/case/Unicode and provider ties without using locale collation or arrival order.

requires: After equal URL and provider, sort integer values numerically and trimmed string values by Unicode code point.
observe: Put conflicting values on the same page; test integer 9 versus 10 and exact-case/Unicode string ordering.

requires: Select the first candidate in the complete ranked list.
observe: Independently compute winner and compare selected flags and field value.

requires: Set field value from the selected candidate; include citation triples from every candidate with that same value, in candidate rank order, and exclude other values' citations.
observe: Use several pages supporting the winner plus competing values and compare exact citation sequence with the filtered candidate list.

requires: Never select lower authority when any higher-authority candidate exists for that field.
observe: Supply one higher-authority value versus many newer lower-authority supporters and inspect the winner.

requires: Run selection over every candidate, not only a top-k subset or initially gathered early winner.
observe: Place a decisive candidate late in discovery/order and verify final rank and selection after collecting the required evidence within budget.

requires: Apply the same latest-read ordering rule to automatic reads while building.

observe: Build populated Stage 1 state, export privately, and import into the exact Stage 2 candidate without transforming the opaque state.

requires: Preserve the already-signed-in browser session across Stage 1 export to Stage 2 import, with old bearer tokens and no manual reauthentication; clarify the pre-upgrade UI setup because Stage 1 required only an API.
observe: Keep one browser context and token signed in before transfer; import the legacy snapshot between requests; continue the existing screen and retry flow using the old session.
readings: The Stage 2 UI must be usable against the Stage 1 API before import/backend replacement, so an actual pre-upgrade browser can sign in and continue without reload.

The guarantee is session/token continuity for an already-initialized browser holding a token present in the Stage 1 export; no backwards-compatible Stage 2 UI-on-Stage 1 API behavior is newly required.

requires: Show imported dossiers in list and dossier screens.
observe: Import populated legacy state while preserving the browser session and inspect list, detail and evidence routes on subsequent reads.

requires: For each imported field reconstruct every value supported by text actually served to its last ready Stage 1 build; create one candidate per supporting page/value, not merely one for the prior selected value; do not substitute text from later failed/running builds.
observe: Prepare a Stage 1 last-ready build with unselected conflicting values and same-value pages, export it, import unchanged, and compare the full expected candidate set using captured served text. Audit whether the frozen legacy export retained enough information; no fallback or import-time refetch is authorized.

requires: Imported excerpts must come from that legacy served text and support their value; use its actual provider; preserve recorded kind/publication metadata or null if unrecorded; set retrieved_at to the dossier's preserved researched_at.
observe: Compare imported candidates with the last-ready Stage 1 provider transcript and exported metadata, including null-kind fallback and offset timestamps.

requires: Recompute imported field selection, status and citations from reconstructed candidates using the Stage 2 rules.
observe: Import legacy conflicting evidence and compare winner, contested/known status and winning-value citation ordering with an independent rank oracle.

requires: Preserve a lost-response request's original key/body replay across export/import; UI retry must recover the original response and display the imported dossier without another build.
observe: Lose a committed Stage 1 research/refresh response in a browser context, transfer state between requests, retry through the UI, and compare original response/key/body and provider count.

observe: Keep the same browser context and current screen through transfer, then act/retry/reread without a manual page reload or new tab.

requires: Replace imported candidate sets with the next ready build's candidates; do not merge legacy and new build evidence; failed builds retain prior ready candidates under inherited rules.
observe: Import, then perform a delayed successful refresh with different evidence and a failed refresh; compare atomic candidate replacement/retention and new retrieved_at values.
